items.title: Roy Carew Interview, 1958-Fall
items.q: according to John Lewis, Tony was playing that thing years before that.

ctx.x: Yeah, that's right, Charles. That's right. Well, he also, I talked to him, the last time I saw him was in New York, and he played the test pressings of those things just before they were issued. And he said that he didn't like the way he did Michigan Water. They insisted he do it that way, and he didn't want to do it that way. And I don't know what he had in mind.

Well, I'll say this about Michigan Water. Clarence Williams had published, claimed it, in 1923 about. Whereas, according to John Lewis, Tony was playing that thing years before that. And as far as the tune itself goes, the verse, I had heard it before that thing, considerably. And I think maybe they got the music of Clarence Williams, and had him follow that to a certain extent, because in a way he does follow, not too closely. But Clarence Williams doubtless picked it up from Tony or from somebody else around…

Well, you know, I think that the much more talented composer than Clarence was the... Oh, that other one. Spencer. Spencer, yeah. Yeah, he was. Spencer was a beautiful thing. Well, Spencer was a pretty well-known piano player in New Orleans too, wasn't he?
